title: Orange Juice No Pulp, Not Fortified, From Concentrate, Refrigerated

content.title: About
content.content: Refrigerated orange juice without pulp is made by removing water from fresh orange juice to create a concentrate, which is later reconstituted and chilled. The juice is not fortified with additional vitamins or minerals, retaining the natural orange flavor but without pulp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Concentrated juice is usually cheaper than freshly squeezed juice while preserving most flavor characteristics.
The absence of pulp makes the beverage smoother and more convenient for quick consumption.
Refrigerated juice has a longer shelf life compared to room‑temperature storage.
In many markets, such juices are sold in 1 L bottles or larger containers.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: The juice provides vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: High water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids in orange juice have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even without added sugar, the juice contains natural sugars, which may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Lack of pulp
items.content: Without pulp, the juice has less dietary fiber, reducing its digestive benefits.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to orange juice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled on its own, or use it in cocktails, smoothies, sauces, and marinades. For added texture, you can mix in pulp or fruit pieces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not keep at room temperature, as this accelerates spoilage.
